images.filename: Siam in 1893, During Rama V's Reign.jpg
images.caption:
This is a map of Thailand during the reign of King Rama V. During this time, Thailand was called Siam and had more territory at the time. This map shows dependencies, monthons, and provinces. The map specifically highlights Siam in yellow.  Notice that this is right before the RS112 incident where Siam had to cede the western bank of the Mekong River. 
Credit:
Shuuranattha "Caphtaain" Ashvajayajita: Designer and Advisor

Tim Plintron, Informant, Advisor, and Revisor

images.filename: French Wolf and Siamese Lamb by John Tenniel 1893.png
images.caption: Illustration title: "The French Wolf and the Siamese Lamb." The French wolf (France) looks menacingly across the Mekong toward the gentle "Siamese lamb" (Thailand). This is political satire about the Franco-Siamese crisis of 1893. It was made by Sir John Tenniel (1820-1914). The artwork was originally published in Punch magazine, 5 August 1893.
